source_text:
τὸ δὲ διὰ τῆς θαλάσσης αὐτοὺς
διελθεῖν ἔοικε κατὰ τοῦτο τοῖς ἡμετέροις, ὅτι ὅπερ ἐκείνοις ἡ διὰ τῆς θαλάσσης
παρέσχε διάβασις, τῶν μὲν πολεμίων αὐτοὺς παντελῶς ἀπαλλάξασα, βεβαίαν δὲ
αὐτοὺς τοῦ λοιποῦ τὴν ἐλευθερίαν δωρησαμένη, τοῦτο ἡμῖν πρὸς τοὺς ἡμετέρους
ἐχθροὺς τὸ βάπτισμα γέγονεν.
thought_title: The sea crossing as a type of baptism's defense
orientation: Gennadius is explaining how the ancient Israelites' passage through the sea prefigured what baptism does for Christians.
pass_a_gloss: Their passing through the sea resembles our things in this respect: what the passage through the sea provided for those people—on the one hand completely freeing them from enemies, on the other hand granting them secure freedom for the future—this baptism has become for us against our enemies.

choices.english: resembles our things in this respect
choices.why: κατὰ τοῦτο points forward to the ὅτι clause; τοῖς ἡμετέροις is neuter plural, referring to Christian realities generally, not persons

choices.term: βεβαίαν δὲ αὐτοὺς τοῦ λοιποῦ τὴν ἐλευθερίαν δωρησαμένη
choices.english: granting them secure freedom for the future
choices.why: βεβαίαν is predicative with ἐλευθερίαν; τοῦ λοιποῦ means 'for the remaining time, henceforth'
rejected: granting them the secure freedom of the rest
bestowing on them the firm liberty of the remainder

choices.why: πρός with accusative here has hostile sense 'against'; ἡμετέρους distinguishes Christian enemies (demonic) from the Egyptians
γέγονεν is perfect, emphasizing the completed state; the article marks baptism as the subject of the identification

pass_b_english: Their passage through the sea resembles our own situation in this respect: what the crossing through the sea provided for them—freeing them completely from their enemies and granting them secure freedom for the future—baptism has become for us against our enemies.
